versions.provenance: 8th edition differentiated (papillary and follicular) thyroid carcinoma staging, rewritten from criteria published on Medscape/public references; interim content pending the licensed content and R1 clinical verification.
versions.introduction:
8th edition staging applies to differentiated thyroid carcinoma (papillary and follicular, including oncocytic/Hurthle cell). The defining feature of the 8th edition is that stage grouping is AGE-DEPENDENT, using an age-at-diagnosis cut-off of 55 years: patients younger than 55 can only be Stage I (M0) or Stage II (M1) no matter the T or N, whereas patients 55 or older follow a conventional T/N/M grouping (I through IVB). Both age tables are provided below and are labelled accordingly.

The 8th edition also revised the T category, removing minimal/microscopic extrathyroidal extension from the T3 definition and splitting T3 into T3a (size-based, > 4 cm) and T3b (gross strap-muscle invasion), which generally down-stages many patients relative to the 7th edition. A key nuance is that post-treatment thyroglobulin trend and the ATA risk-of-recurrence category complement anatomic stage in guiding surveillance and therapy. Anaplastic and medullary thyroid carcinomas use separate staging systems.

t.label: Tumour <= 2 cm in greatest dimension, limited to the thyroid
Tumour <= 1 cm, limited to the thyroid
Tumour > 1 cm and <= 2 cm, limited to the thyroid
Tumour > 2 cm and <= 4 cm, limited to the thyroid
Tumour > 4 cm limited to the thyroid, OR gross extrathyroidal extension invading only the strap muscles
Tumour > 4 cm, limited to the thyroid
Gross extrathyroidal extension invading only the strap muscles (sternohyoid, sternothyroid, thyrohyoid, or omohyoid), from a tumour of any size
Advanced disease with gross extrathyroidal extension beyond the strap muscles
Gross extrathyroidal extension invading subcutaneous soft tissue, larynx, trachea, esophagus, or recurrent laryngeal nerve, from a tumour of any size
Gross extrathyroidal extension invading prevertebral fascia, or encasing the carotid artery or mediastinal vessels, from a tumour of any size

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
No evidence of regional lymph node metastasis
One or more cytologically or histologically confirmed benign lymph nodes
No radiologic or clinical evidence of locoregional lymph node metastasis
Metastasis to level VI or VII (pretracheal, paratracheal, prelaryngeal/Delphian, or upper mediastinal) nodes; unilateral or bilateral
Metastasis to unilateral, bilateral, or contralateral lateral neck nodes (levels I, II, III, IV, or V) or to retropharyngeal nodes

stageGroups.basis: Age at diagnosis < 55 years with no distant metastasis is Stage I regardless of T and N.
Age at diagnosis < 55 years with any distant metastasis is Stage II.
Age >= 55, tumour <= 2 cm, node-negative, no metastasis.
Age >= 55, tumour > 2 to <= 4 cm, node-negative, no metastasis.
Age >= 55, tumour <= 2 cm with regional nodal metastasis.
Age >= 55, tumour > 2 to <= 4 cm with regional nodal metastasis.
Age >= 55, tumour > 4 cm limited to thyroid, any nodal status.
Age >= 55, gross strap-muscle invasion, any nodal status.
Age >= 55, gross extrathyroidal extension into soft tissue/larynx/trachea/esophagus/recurrent laryngeal nerve, any nodal status.
Age >= 55, extension to prevertebral fascia or encasement of carotid/mediastinal vessels, any nodal status.

versions.regionalNodes: Regional nodes are the central compartment (level VI and VII: pretracheal, paratracheal, prelaryngeal/Delphian, and upper mediastinal), the lateral cervical nodes (levels I to V), and the retropharyngeal nodes.
versions.histologicGrade: Differentiated thyroid carcinoma is not conventionally assigned a numeric grade; histologic subtype and features such as tall-cell, columnar, hobnail, or solid variants, and the newer high-grade differentiated category, carry prognostic significance.
versions.histopathologicTypes: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (and variants: classic, follicular, tall-cell, columnar, hobnail, and others), follicular thyroid carcinoma, and oncocytic (Hurthle cell) carcinoma. Medullary and anaplastic (undifferentiated) carcinomas are staged separately.
prognosticFactors: Age at diagnosis (the 55-year cut-off drives stage grouping)
Gross extrathyroidal extension and completeness of resection
Aggressive histologic variant (tall-cell, columnar, hobnail, solid)
Response to therapy and post-treatment thyroglobulin trend
ATA risk-of-recurrence category and BRAF/TERT mutation status
